defect.site: the cross-universe branch called resolver.resolve_exact(equivalence_ref) on a parameter typed Any and accepted the returned object's ref
why_exact_lookup_is_not_adjudication: resolve_exact returns whatever relation carries the requested ref
it does not require the relation decision to be AUTHORIZED
it does not check the relation KIND
it does not check that the relation binds the requested universe PAIR
it does not check operation scope, effective scope, target use, or authority
the comparison afterwards only compared the returned object's ref to the requested ref, which a stub can satisfy trivially

reproduced_before_any_change.duck_typed_stub_resolver: TEMPORAL_DIRECTIONAL_CLAIM_AUTHORIZED (defect: a stub mimicking resolve_exact admitted the pair)
reproduced_before_any_change.comparison_of_interest: the same fixture with a GENUINE owner-adjudicated relation did NOT produce the positive state, while the stub did -- the split brain HQ218 described

repair.principle: F7 consumes a real positive source-relation OWNER decision from the existing adopted owner path. It creates no equivalence authority.
repair.mechanism: F7 calls SourceRelationResolver.require(...) with the exact relation kind, the exact universe pair, the exact operation and effective scope, the exact governed-use target_use, the presented relation ref, and the expected authority operation. require() runs the owner's decide() and raises unless the decision is AUTHORIZED.
owner_side_validation_obtained_for_free: the relation's source_universe_refs must equal the requested pair
target_use must match the governed use F7 requires
the authority must actually authorize the relation, with the expected operation
repair.resolver_type_enforced: the resolver must be an actual pre553_source_relations.SourceRelationResolver. A duck-typed object that merely mimics resolve_exact can no longer stand in for the owner decision path. This is why isinstance is checked before require is called.
repair.constant_note: these are requirements F7 imposes when it asks the owner, not authorities F7 creates; the owner still decides and may refuse
repair.important_semantic_correction: F7 requires the relation to be adjudicated for the GOVERNED USE, not for the relation's own ref. The prior lawful fixture built the relation with target_use=relation_ref.object_id, so under the corrected contract it correctly refused. The fixture was updated to adjudicate for the governed use. A relation authorized only for itself must not admit a governed use, and this is now enforced.
repair.adopted_owner_unmodified: rawlsing_next/pre553_source_relations.py was NOT modified; its blob is unchanged and no production or court file outside the two commissioned files was touched
repair.import_posture: F7 imports the adopted owner as a MODULE and reads SourceRelationResolver and FORBIDDEN_BACKFILL_TARGET_STATES as attributes. A from-import of the constant was tried first and reverted: it broke the backfill guard's live-surface liveness proof, which monkeypatches the owner module and requires F7 to observe the change. Module import keeps the module imported exactly once AND keeps the frozen surface read live.
repair.consequence_for_the_import_census: test_module_imports_no_f8_and_no_new_family pins the exact internal import set. Because pre553_source_relations was already in that set and the function-local backfill import already existed, a second import of the same module would have produced a duplicate entry and failed the census. The module import posture resolves this without widening the pinned set.

wrong_relation_kind.handling: the adopted factory refuses to authorize OVERLAP_NON_DUPLICATION under a SOURCE_EQUIVALENCE snapshot, so wrong-kind material cannot even be constructed as AUTHORIZED. F7 additionally pins the relation kind it asks the owner about, so a wrong-kind relation admitted by some other authority path is still refused.

targeted_break.method: with a genuinely DENIED relation the pair is refused; monkeypatching the owner's require() to report AUTHORIZED makes the SAME fixture produce the positive receipt
targeted_break.proves: the owner's decision is load-bearing. If F7 fell back to exact object lookup, patching require() would change nothing and this witness would fail.
targeted_break.note: this is the strongest of the three targeted breaks because the only variable is the owner decision itself

no_equivalence_creation: F7 asks; it never grants. No equivalence authority, relation state, relation kind, or authority kind was added.
hq217_tests_preserved: test_witness_cross_universe_is_derived_from_bound_universes -- still produces the positive receipt, now through real owner adjudication
